title: Leveraging Sparse Linear Layers for Debuggable Deep Networks

bias_targets.methodology: Inspecting deep features via LIME-based word clouds in sparse decision layers and performing counterfactual text modifications (e.g., appending religious terms like 'christianity' to sentences) to evaluate prediction flips in toxicity classification.
Analyzing highly weighted deep features using word cloud visualizations to detect if nationality-related words are spuriously used by the model as evidence for or against toxicity.
Examining deep features via word clouds to identify whether sexual identity terms (e.g., 'gay', 'homosexuality') are disproportionately weighted to predict toxicity or non-toxicity.
Visualizing the model's sparse decision layer features to observe if racial and ethnic terms (e.g., 'black', 'white', 'caucasian') are relied upon as evidence in toxic comment classifiers.
